best_for: Music collectors who keep their albums on a Plex Media Server and want a dedicated player with gapless playback, loudness leveling and smart radio on the desktop.

points.title: Needs your own Plex server
points.text: Plexamp plays the music library on a Plex Media Server. Plex says plainly that you need one to use it with your own collection; it is not a store or a streaming catalog.

points.title: Free player, good basics
points.text: Without paying you get gapless playback, loudness leveling, Sweet Fades transitions, pre-caching, smart playlists and stations, visualizers, Chromecast and AirPlay.

points.title: The smart features need Plex Pass
points.text: Downloads, lyrics, the ten-band equalizer, sample rate matching, track and album radio, Guest DJ, Sonic Sage and sonically similar mixes are reserved for Plex Pass members. Headless Plexamp on a Raspberry Pi is also a Pass feature.

points.title: Remote music is not paywalled
points.text: Plex charges for streaming personal video away from home, but its plans page says that rule does not apply to music streamed to Plexamp.

points.title: The Linux build lags behind
points.text: The Flathub Flatpak is verified as Plex's own but is x64 only, and it sits at 4.13.2 while Windows and macOS are on 4.50.20. If you need a recent feature on Linux, check that the Flatpak has caught up.

points.title: Installers and history
points.text: Windows installers come in x64 and Arm64 and install per user, so no administrator rights are needed. macOS has Intel and Apple silicon builds. The Windows listing keeps 55 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
